nodes.title: Fleetbase installation
nodes.body:
I'm having problems installing Fleetbase.

The communication between the Frontend and Backend.

Does anyone have a step-by-step guide to a safe and efficient installation?

I tried installing it outside of Docker, and now I'm looking at the option of installing it with a Docker container. What's the best option considering good performance and stability?
Hello, I'm having trouble installing via docker. At step 8, it issues an error copying console files. Can you tell me how to fix this problem?

The only problem I have is that although the containers are up, and I manage to perform the migration when I try to create an account to use the program through :4200/auth the create account button does not work so I can not configure or advance from that screen.

The installation and configuration of fleetbase is an absolute disaster whichever way you look at it. I'm running into the same problems. Docker is always the best answer.

Version mismatch and manual edits required at multiple points. Which causes breaks in the install/deployment, which means steps are missed and need to be addressed as they come up when things aren't working. 

The steps I used to get it up and running a few days ago, don't work today either!

Let's just follow the simple way via [[https://docs.fleetbase.io/getting-started/install/with-cli](https://docs.fleetbase.io/getting-started/install/with-cli)]

First, we'll need to add a step before step 1. Lets call it something like "first step 1: install node.js via instructions at https://nodejs.org/en/download"

Now we can follow step 1 and step 2 in the docs.

_But alas, step 3, we cannot wait for the installation to finish because it didn't finish. It's broken._

**What's broken?** 
MYSQL of course. It can't start because it doesn't have the proper permissions to access the bind mounts. Which means no database, and no seeding.

The uid and group of the user is 999:999 as you can find from `docker exec -it fleetbase_database_1 id mysql` once your container is up and running of course.

Could be a SELinux issue because if you change the uid and permissions all you want, it doesn't work. Instead I took the quick way out and created a volume mount by commenting out the volume binds in `docker-compose.yml` and adding my own volume mount in `docker-compose-overrride.yml` 

```
services:
  database:
    volumes:
        - db_data:/var/lib/mysql

volumes:
   db_data:
```

We can now try to build with `docker compose up -d --build`, but in my case I needed to comment out a line [21] in the `console/Dockerfile` that was `COPY .npmr[c] ./` in order to continue.

Today trying to create a new build I had to change line [2] from `FROM node:18.15.0-alpine as builder` to `FROM node:22-alpine as builder` in order to continue. Maybe a cache thing, maybe new code pulled from repo.. don't know and don't care.

So now on the surface, everything looks to be built and up and running. But we can't create an account or install anything (_There's no database because the seeding didn't complete_).

You'll need to manually execute the `deploy.sh` script [https://github.com/fleetbase/fleetbase/blob/main/api/deploy.sh](https://github.com/fleetbase/fleetbase/blob/main/api/deploy.sh) or run the php artisan commands within your application container manually.

`docker exec -it fleetbase_application_1 bash -c  "./deploy.sh"`

Then I could finish the creation of an account and get into the fleetbase app. I downloaded and configured the navigator app and all is well from an internal ip networking perspective.

nodes.title: Errors when running deploy.sh when using Cloud SQL as DB
nodes.body:
Hello Fleetbase team!

I'm currently attempting to deploy Fleetbase and it's constituent services as applications on Google Kubernetes Engine. So far I've had luck deploying:
- Application
- Cache
- Scheduler
- Socket

Database and Redis are to be Cloud SQL and Memorystore respectively. The Cache, Scheduler and Application pods have their respective containers + a Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar container.

I'm running into a bit of an issue though, specifically when running the migrations script and I'm wondering if there's any extra considerations I need to take into account when using MySQL on Cloud SQL for my DB. Error:
```
In Connection.php line 829:

  SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 6125 Failed to add the foreign key constraint. Missing unique key for constraint 'model_has_permissions_permission_id_foreign' in the referenced table 'permissions' (Connection: mysql, SQL: alter ta
  ble `model_has_permissions` add constraint `model_has_permissions_permission_id_foreign` foreign key (`permission_id`) references `permissions` (`id`) on delete cascade)


In Connection.php line 587:

  SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 6125 Failed to add the foreign key constraint. Missing unique key for constraint 'model_has_permissions_permission_id_foreign' in the referenced table 'permissions'
```

I've tried manually fixing each error that comes up by performing SQL surgery in Cloud Shell, but now I'm just wondering if there's something specific about Cloud SQL that's bugging this out and preventing the migrations script from running smoothly?

If it counts: running all the services entirely on my machine as Docker containers runs perfectly fine, and I am able to exec into the Application container and run the deploy.sh script successfully and to completion.

Thank you for your time!! ­ƒÖÅ­ƒÅ╝

The error you're encountering (`SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 6125`) is common when using **Cloud SQL for MySQL** (specifically version 8.0+) with Laravel-based applications like Fleetbase. It typically occurs because of how Cloud SQL handles default storage engines, character sets, or specific foreign key checks during concurrent migrations.

Since the migrations work locally but fail on Cloud SQL, here is the recommended approach to resolve this:

### 1. Verify Engine and Collation Consistency
Cloud SQL sometimes defaults to `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`, whereas local Docker environments might use `utf8mb4_unicode_ci`. If the `permissions` table and the `model_has_permissions` table have different collations or engines, MySQL will fail to create the foreign key even if the columns look identical.

Before running the migration, ensure your Cloud SQL instance is configured correctly:
*   **Storage Engine:** Ensure it is `InnoDB`.
*   **Character Set:** Use `utf8mb4`.

### 2. Disable Foreign Key Checks for the Initial Migration
If you are performing a fresh installation or a large migration batch, Cloud SQL's strictness can cause race conditions where a child table is processed before the parent index is fully committed. You can wrap the migration command to temporarily ignore these constraints.

Exec into your Application pod and run:
```bash
php artisan tinker --execute="DB::statement('SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0;');"
php artisan migrate --force
php artisan tinker --execute="DB::statement('SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=1;');"
```

### 3. Check for Migration State Corruption
If you have been doing "SQL surgery" manually, your `migrations` table in Cloud SQL might be out of sync with the actual schema. This prevents Laravel from knowing which migrations are actually "complete."

1.  **Wipe the database** (if this is a fresh setup) to ensure a clean slate:
    ```bash
    php artisan db:wipe
    ```
2.  **Run the deploy script again.** By using `db:wipe`, you ensure that `permissions` is created with its unique keys before `model_has_permissions` attempts to reference it.

### 4. Adjust Cloud SQL Flags
If the issue persists, check your Cloud SQL instance **Flags**. Some managed environments restrict index creation if `foreign_key_checks` or `sql_require_primary_key` (if enabled) are conflicting. Ensure `sql_require_primary_key` is set to **OFF** if you are using Fleetbase versions that rely on many-to-many pivot tables without explicit primary keys.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Since you are using a Sidecar Proxy, ensure your `DB_HOST` in your Kubernetes Secret/ConfigMap is set to `127.0.0.1` and not a private IP, as the proxy handles the tunnel to Cloud SQL locally within the pod.

Are you using MySQL 8.0 or 5.7 on your Cloud SQL instance, and did you notice if the `permissions` table was successfully created with a primary key before the failure?

nodes.title: API Endpoint/Strategy for Integrating Hardware Trackers
nodes.body:
As title says, I have a fleet of devices with existing hardware trackers that use the H02 protocol. I am happy to write the implementation for this, but was trying to figure out what the best approach would be for sending data via the API into Fleetbase.

Example:

Hardware Tracker -(h02)> My Middleware -(_unknown method_)> Fleetbase

I am trying to out how to take the data from my middleware (to interpret the H02 data) and dump it into Fleetbase so it knows where the respective vehicle is.

Any thoughts?

While you're building out the middleware pipeline, [Moveet](https://github.com/ivannovazzi/moveet) might be handy for testing the integration end-to-end before your actual hardware is available.

It's an open-source fleet simulator that generates realistic vehicle position data using A* pathfinding on real road networks (OpenStreetMap/GeoJSON). It streams positions over WebSocket and exposes a REST API, so you can simulate what your H02 middleware would be pushing to Fleetbase ÔÇö without needing physical trackers attached to vehicles.

Useful for iterating on your middleware logic and validating Fleetbase's ingestion before hardware is in the loop.

nodes.title: Request for Quotation (RFQ): Fleetbase Website Revamp
nodes.body:
One of our milestone goals is to completely revamp the official website and documentation for Fleetbase. The new site should clearly communicate our product, features, and vision. WeÔÇÖre opening this task up to the world and inviting quotations from web designers and developers who are up for the challenge.

Please read the RFQ below, and if youÔÇÖre interested, send the required information via email or reply directly to this discussion.

**Date Issued:** July 15th, 2025
**Company:** Fleetbase Pte Ltd  
**Website:** [https://fleetbase.io](https://fleetbase.io)

---

## 1. Overview

Fleetbase is seeking proposals from qualified web design and development vendors to **revamp our official website**. The new site should serve as a **conversion-focused**, product-driven platform showcasing our open-source logistics operating system and flagship extensions. It should reflect modern design standards, reinforce FleetbaseÔÇÖs brand identity, and streamline user acquisition.

Our **current website is built on [Webflow](https://webflow.com)**. We are open to:
- Continuing with Webflow,
- Migrating to [Framer](https://framer.com), or
- A **custom-built solution** using modern frameworks (e.g., Astro, Next.js), **provided it is easy to maintain** and includes:
  - A **visual CMS or markdown editor for content/docs**
  - A **cloud-based CMS** (e.g., Sanity, Storyblok, Contentful)

**We will not accept proposals that use WordPress.**

---

## 2. Goals and Objectives

- Create a clean, modern, high-performance website
- Highlight our **products**, **extensions**, and **SDKs** with persuasive landing pages
- Integrate **documentation**, **API reference**, and **markdown-based guides**
- Offer a **blog** powered by a cloud CMS
- Add a **checkout interface** for services and commercial licenses
- Present our **AGPL license** and commercial license offerings clearly
- Include a **Developer section** with code examples, SDKs, and API tools
- Ensure ease of maintenance via a CMS or visual editor

---

## 3. Scope of Work

Design and develop a fully responsive and conversion-optimized website with:

- ~20 modular landing pages
- Blog powered by a headless CMS
- Markdown editor interface for guides/docs
- API reference integration (e.g., Redoc)
- Checkout interface (e.g., Stripe)
- Licensing page with pricing and funnel to checkout
- SEO, accessibility, performance optimization
- CMS handoff documentation

---

## 4. Website Page Structure

### **Home**
- Clear value prop and feature highlights
- CTA for developers and enterprise customers

---

### **Products**

Each product below must have a dedicated landing page with screenshots, benefits, and CTA.

1. **Navigator App** ÔÇô Driver app with real-time location tracking, order routing, proof of delivery, chat, fuel/issue reports  
2. **Storefront App** ÔÇô Native app for Storefront, supports checkout, product listings, and multi-vendor marketplaces  
3. **Storefront** ÔÇô Headless commerce extension with logistics-first design  
4. **Customer Portal** ÔÇô Portal for end-users to place, view, and track orders  
5. **FleetOps** ÔÇô Flagship TMS & fleet management system for last-mile to freight  
6. **Pallet** ÔÇô Inventory and warehouse management (WMS) extension  
7. **Ledger** ÔÇô Accounting and invoicing suite for logistics operations  
8. **Framework / Developer Tools** ÔÇô Developer UI to manage API keys, webhooks, logs  
9. **Extensions** ÔÇô Overview of modular architecture and extension system

---

### **Developer Page**
- Overview of developer features
- Embed code examples using markdown/blocks
- List available SDKs (JS, PHP, Node, etc.)
- Links to API docs and GitHub repos
- Highlight open-source nature and AGPL license

---

### **Licensing Page**
- Clear explanation of the **AGPL license**
- Detailed overview of **Commercial License**:
  - Features unlocked
  - Use-case eligibility
  - Pricing tiers (e.g., Annual, Monthly, Version Lock)
- Funnel to **checkout/purchase flow** for licensing

---

### **Services**
1. Custom Extension Development  
2. On-Premise / Cloud Deployment  
3. Professional Training

---

### **About**
- Company mission and team
- Partners and community contributors
- Contact information

---

## 5. Technical Requirements

- Preferred platforms: **Webflow** or **Framer**
- Acceptable custom stacks: **Astro**, **Next.js**, or similar SSG with CMS integration
- **Must NOT use WordPress**
- Markdown-based documentation UI or Git-integrated docs system
- Headless/cloud CMS for blog and content
- API reference integration (Redoc, Stoplight, etc.)
- Checkout interface (Stripe, LemonSqueezy, etc.)
- Mobile-first design, performance-optimized
- SEO and analytics integrations (GA, Plausible, etc.)
- Multi-language optional (bonus)

---

## 6. Design Inspiration

Design aesthetic should take cues from:

- [https://medusajs.com](https://medusajs.com)
- [https://saleor.io](https://saleor.io)
- [https://stripe.com](https://stripe.com) ÔÇô especially navigation
- [https://www.metabase.com](https://www.metabase.com)

---

## 7. Submission Requirements

All applicants **must** provide:

- A portfolio with similar projects
- A brief description of your **proposed stack or platform**
- Your **approach to the build** (Webflow/Framer/custom? How would you implement docs, blog, licensing funnel?)
- Estimated **timeline**
- **Pricing breakdown**
- Any assumptions or exclusions

Proposals **without portfolio and build approach will not be considered.**

---

## 8. Submission Deadline

August 10th, 2025

---

## 9. Contact

To submit or ask questions:

­ƒôº Email: **website.revamp@fleetbase.io**  
­ƒÆ¼ Or reply directly to this **GitHub Discussion Thread** of the RFQ.

---

in docker env, i get the error message:

then i try to edit docker-compose.yml and add "privileged: true" in service "database", still not work

Try changing the mysql volume from a bind mount to a named mount so that docker can manage the volume.

volumes:

database:

Issue resolved, I was running a very old docker version. Docker version 1.13.1, build 4ef4b30/1.13.1, so I upgraded it to Docker version 24.0.7, build afdd53b with the following steps:


Removing your existing Docker version

Remove the Docker version installed by OpenShift and Cloud Pak for Data by running the following commands. These commands will not leave your system in an unrecoverable state.

sudo yum remove docker \
                  docker-client \
                  docker-client-latest \
                  docker-common \
                  docker-latest \
                  docker-latest-logrotate \
                  docker-logrotate \
                  docker-engine

If you see messages that an item can't be removed, the reason is because not all items are installed. These messages can be ignored.
Updating servers with internet access

    On a node with internet access running Docker run the following command. Note: Your user account must have sudo privileges for this command to work.

    sudo yum-config-manager \
        --add-repo \
        https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo

If you have root access you can run this command instead:

yum-config-manager \
    --add-repo \
    https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo

Run the following command to install the latest Docker version from the repository.

yum install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io

nodes.title: Proposal: Monorepo for Fleetbase Extensions
nodes.body:
Currently considering combining extensions into a single repository. Currently backend and frontend for a single extension is split into their own proejct/repo. For example `fleetops` has two repo's `fleetbase/fleetops-api` and `fleetbase/fleetops-engine` - After this proposal fleetops would be available in a single `fleetbase/fleetops` repo.

The idea of combining repositories for a frontend and backend application into a single monorepo is not uncommon and has both advantages and disadvantages.

**Advantages of a Monorepo**

1. Unified Development Experience: Developers can pull one repository and have everything they need to work on a feature that may require changes in both frontend and backend.
2. Simplified CI/CD: Having a single repository can make CI/CD pipelines easier to manage and configure.
3. Atomic Commits: You can update the frontend and backend in one commit, ensuring consistency.
4. Shared Resources: Easier to share common configurations, libraries, and modules.
5. Dependency Management: Easier to manage cross-project dependencies.

**Disadvantages of a Monorepo**

1. Learning Curve: Developers need to understand both frontend and backend project structures and how they interact.
2. Build Complexity: It may be more complicated to only build/test/deploy what has changed.
3. Large Repository: Over time, the repository may grow large, and cloning or pulling changes may become slower.
4. Tooling: Not all package managers and build tools play nicely with a monorepo structure.

While I do believe the advantages far outweigh the disadvantages I wanted to share this proposal for feedback.

**Here is an example of the new extension monorepo structure.**
```/fleetops
|-- /client
|   |-- /addon
|   |-- /app
|   |-- /config
|   |-- /tests
|   |-- /translations
|   |-- /vendor
|   |-- ember-cli-build.js
|   |-- package.json
|
|-- /server
|   |-- /config
|   |-- /data
|   |-- /migrations
|   |-- /src
|   |-- /tests
|   |-- composer.json
|   |-- phpunit.xml
|   |-- .php_cs
|
|-- /shared
|   |-- /common-config
|   |-- /common-libraries
|
|-- README.md
|-- .gitignore```

This new extension offers effortless management of users, groups, roles, and policies. Your power to oversee and regulate access within your instance has never been this easy and secure!

2. *Advanced Permissions and Policies Management:* Amplifying our commitment to offer you comprehensive control over your operations, this release enables robust management of permissions and policies for extensions. With this, you can define permissions with utmost granularity, ensuring your team members have precisely the level of access they require.

3. *Squashing Bugs:* We've heard your feedback and tackled those pesky bugs impacting driver creation and updating. With these issues squashed, you're all set to enjoy a smoother, error-free interaction with Fleetbase.

4. *Country Select Gets a Makeover:* In Fleetbase v0.1.3, we've amped up the aesthetics with styling improvements for the Country Select function.

5. *OSRM Routing Engine Patch:* To enable more regions for routing, we've patched the OSRM Routing Engine Host ENV `OSRM_SERVER` variable to point to the correct server. This little patch enables routing for: Nigeria, Uganda, South Africa, UK, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Denmark, Netherlands, France, Pakistan, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand

We're just getting started! We are continually working on refining and enhancing Fleetbase to become the ultimate logistics platform. We eagerly look forward to your feedback on these new updates. Your insights are invaluable in shaping the future of Fleetbase.

Stay tuned for more game-changing updates coming your way, and as always, thank you for being a pivotal part of our incredible community!
